summary: Sweetman Mountain tower in Granville MA: 65-ft wooden tripod first operated 1931, staffed to 1962, sold on eBay 2003, footings only per 2005 survey.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire site says the 65-ft wooden tower was first operated in 1931 and was staffed until 1962. It also describes a 1915 40-ft Aermotor (formerly the Becket Mountain tower) and a 1934 60-ft Aermotor built by a CCC crew from camp 64. It does not say how those Aermotors relate to the 65-ft tower. It says 'this tower' was sold on eBay in 2003 and that only footings remain of it, without naming the structure. The Granville Fire Department history mentions only the 65-foot wooden tower. The story gives the 1962 end of staffing for the 65-foot tower and leaves the other structures' fates open.

notes_for_editor: Record fields (Hampden county, 443.5 m elevation, gone, tower) match the sources; no correction. The 2005 footings finding comes from the Forest Fire site alone. FFLA Massachusetts Facebook posts about Sweetman Mountain (remains, a 1950s observer photo, a removal post, a recovered photo of the tower) appeared in search results, but fetch returned only titles, so no claims from them are used and no photo is added. A lead for the editor: the FFLA post titled as a recovered photo of the Sweetman Mountain tower may carry a usable image, if its license can be confirmed. Fact-check 2026-10-10: the earlier story said the site did not make clear which structure stood until 1962; the page says the 65-ft tower was staffed until 1962, so that sentence was corrected. The phrase 'stood above Granville' was removed as unsupported by the sources.
